evidence.claim: Cardholder C11891 denies the $292.36 charge (txn 3478782), states their online purchases are typically under $50, and does not recognise the hotmail.com address on the transaction; they asked for the card to be blocked.
Flagged amount $292.36 is 6.55x the 180-day mean of $44.66 and exceeds the card's all-time maximum of $121.32 (amount z ~9.8) across 35 baseline transactions.
Prior closed case CC-4160 on the same card C11891-K1 was confirmed CNP fraud ($90.54, 2016-09-29), showing this card number has been compromised before and reported by the same cardholder.
The real-time model scored txn 3478782 at 0.79; a score alone is only a reason to look, but it is consistent with the other signals here.

Device profile 'Trident/7.0 | unknown | ie 11.0 for tablet | unknown' appears on 46 cards all-time / 14 in window, including cards C11923-K2, C05031-K2, C11509-K2, C13171-K2 with many confirmed CNP/card-testing cases; however it is also 8 of this card's own 35 baseline transactions, so it is treated as a common browser string, not a shared-origin link.

Policy R2: when the customer denies the transaction, block the card and create a case; exposure of $292.36 is below the $1,000 reporting threshold and no genuine shared-origin link is established, so no regulatory report is required.

case.summary: Transaction 3478782 ($292.36, online, product C) on card C11891-K1 is 6.55x the cardholder's 180-day mean and above their all-time card maximum, on an account whose normal activity is 35 small online purchases averaging $44.66. The cardholder was asked to validate and denies the charge, saying the amount and the hotmail.com address are not theirs. The same card already carries a confirmed CNP fraud case (CC-4160, $90.54, September 2016), indicating repeat exposure of the number. The rare-device link to heavily fraud-affected cards is discounted because that browser string is part of this card's own routine history and appears on 46 cards all-time. Single-transaction card-not-present fraud: block the card, create a case, reverse the charge; exposure $292.36 is under the reporting threshold and no coordinated origin is proven, so no SAR.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: The cardholder does not recognize the $292.36 charge and denies making it, noting it is far larger than anything they normally spend online (their purchases are typically under $50) and that the hotmail.com address is not theirs. They requested the card be blocked and the charge reversed.

initial.reason: R1: p=0.45 is not decisive; verify before any block
§3a: a case is opened whenever evidence is requested

final.reason: R2: customer denies the transaction; exposure $292.36 <= $2,500 -> L1
R2/§3a: open the fraud case and write it to the graph

next_best_actions.what_changed: The customer validation reply came back as a denial, converting a single-signal anomaly (probability 0.45) into confirmed card-not-present fraud at 0.88 under policy R2.

sar.reason: Case only, no report: fraud with exposure $292.36 <= $1,000, no shared device/region link and a documented pattern, so no §3a condition holds.

stop_reason: Decisive: p=0.88 with 4 independent signals and evidence confidence 0.94 (policy §6). A verification response settled the question: the cardholder denies the charge, and with the amount anomaly and the prior confirmed fraud on this card the evidence exceeds 0.85 on at least two independent signals. Further steps would not change the decision.
